title: Condensed and continuous coefficient presentations of embedded lattices
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with topological valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be any scheme and work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention] on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $A_X,E_X$ for the pulled-back condensed ring objects [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], with the inclusion induced by $A\hookrightarrow E$, and use module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Write $A_X^c(U)=C(|U|,A)$ and $E_X^c(U)=C(|U|,E)$ for the continuous-function coefficient sheaves. Let $L$ be an $E_X$-module pro-étale locally free of finite rank, and let $L^c$ denote its transport to $E_X^c$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

The canonical coefficient comparisons $A_X\simeq A_X^c$ and $E_X\simeq E_X^c$ intertwine the integral inclusion and identify $A_X[1/\ell]$ with $E_X$. For every site object $U$, they induce a bijection, compatible with all restrictions, between embedded locally finite free $A_U$-submodules $N\subseteq L|_U$ with $N[1/\ell]=L|_U$ and isomorphism classes of pairs $(M,\alpha)$ with $M$ a locally finite free $A_U^c$-module and $\alpha:E_U^c\otimes_{A_U^c}M\xrightarrow{\sim}L^c|_U$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Equivalence of pairs means an integral isomorphism intertwining $\alpha$. The inverse bijection takes the embedded image of $m\mapsto\alpha(1\otimes m)$ and transports it back. The localization/scalar-extension identification is $m/\ell^n\mapsto\ell^{-n}\otimes m$, with inverse $(a/\ell^n)\otimes m\mapsto am/\ell^n$, locally on the site. On any trivialization $L|_U\simeq E_U^r$ the class of $(g(A_U^c)^r,\alpha_g)$, where $\alpha_g:E_U^c\otimes_{A_U^c}g(A_U^c)^r\xrightarrow{\sim}(E_U^c)^r\simeq L^c|_U$ is the scalar-extension isomorphism induced by the inclusion $g(A_U^c)^r\subseteq(E_U^c)^r$ and the transported trivialization, corresponds to $gA_U^r$ for every $g\in\operatorname{GL}_r(E)$, including $r=0$.

proof.text: Apply the continuous-ring universe comparison to A and E. The transpose under the inverse-image adjunction computes by precomposition of continuous functions. Naturality in the coefficient inclusion gives the commuting square.

Construct a regular additive telescope on compact profinite tests with leg a |-> a/ell^n. The norm-unit-ball description of the integral coefficient ring and compact boundedness produce a denominator for every continuous E-valued function. Injectivity of the subtype inclusion proves the filtered-colimit equality relation. Sheafification and inverse image preserve this colimit; transport through the coefficient comparisons gives the scheme cocone. Its zeroth-leg formula and the cocone recurrence, cancelling ell in E pointwise, give every nth-leg formula.
Apply the slice scalar-extension fraction theorem to each integral module M. Its forward and balanced inverse formulas are precisely the two displayed normalization equations.

For a pair P, construct its image as the sectionwise linear-map range of pairEmbedding. The coefficient inclusion is pointwise injective, so the already proved lattice-image locality theorem identifies the pair module with this range presheaf. Transport its sheaf and finite local freeness properties along that explicit isomorphism. Local numerator representatives of the inverse rationalization show that this image is full.

Given an embedded lattice N, its explicit submodule sheaf and the canonical full-lattice rationalization give an integral pair. The unit normalization identifies its image sectionwise with N, proving surjectivity. Equality of embedded lattices is equality of submodule families by proof irrelevance. The pair image classification theorem therefore identifies the kernel of the constructed surjection with equivalence of pairs.

The constructed submodule is the sectionwise range, so its image formula holds directly. Use the existing restriction-image theorem for slice compatibility. The existing matrix integral-pair existence theorem supplies a pair for every frame and matrix, and its image equation yields the exact matrix label, including rank zero.
